The History of Christmas

3D storyboard: 61 shots in 7 acts, about 8 minutes. Flurry the snowman guides the story from Bethlehem to Santa and ends with "Happy Christmas!". Frames are draft renders from the real scenes. Full video goes out 24 Dec, 00:00 IST.

Act 0 Christmas Eve 24 DECEMBER · 47s

0.1 4s

Today is the 24th of December. Christmas Eve.

Snowy village at night, warm windows; a snowdrift wobbles and Flurry the snowman pushes up out of it, shakes off snow and blinks awake

Camera: slow push in on the snowdrift · Sound: soft wind, sleigh bells, snow puff

0.2 11s

Well, it is on the day this video goes up. If you are watching later, hello, future person! Tell us in the comments what happened.

Flurry hops toward camera and waves with a twig arm; a speech-bubble comment floats up beside him

Camera: gentle orbit around Flurry · Sound: boing hops, chime

0.3 7s

Tomorrow, the whole world celebrates Christmas. Even in countries where most people are not Christian.

A night globe slowly turning in space, warm lights twinkle on across it one by one

Camera: slow rotation, push in · Sound: twinkle chimes

0.4 7s

Japan is a great example. Very few Christians, but trees, lights, gifts and parties everywhere.

Flurry slides along a lantern-lit street with a giant lit tree, paper lanterns sway

Camera: lateral dolly with Flurry · Sound: city bells, light crowd

chip: JAPAN LOVES CHRISTMAS

0.5 7s

But here is the twist. Jesus was probably not born on the 25th of December.

Flurry holds up a big calendar page DEC 25; it flips over to a giant question mark; Flurry's eyes go wide

Camera: quick push in · Sound: page flip, comic sting

0.6 7s

And the tree, the mistletoe, the carols, the feast? Most of them are older than Christmas itself.

Tree, mistletoe, songbook and roast slide in around Flurry one by one; his carrot nose droops in shock

Camera: orbit around Flurry · Sound: four whooshes

0.7 6s

So grab a hot chocolate. Let's find out where Christmas really comes from.

Flurry jumps on a red sled and zooms down a snowy hill past pine trees, hot chocolate steaming

Camera: fast tracking shot beside the sled · Sound: sled whoosh, music lifts

slam: THE HISTORY OF CHRISTMAS

Act 1 The First Story 1ST CENTURY · 45s

1.1 5s

Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity.

Night over Bethlehem, flat-roofed stone houses, palms, one huge bright star

Camera: crane down from the star · Sound: night insects, soft choir pad

1.2 11s

Christians believe he is the son of God. And almost all historians agree he was a real person, who lived about two thousand years ago.

An old book opens on a reading stand by lamplight; Flurry peeks over it, nodding

Camera: slow push in · Sound: page turn

chip: A REAL HISTORICAL PERSON

1.3 9s

The Gospels of Luke and Matthew tell the story. Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem, for a census.

Joseph walks leading a grey donkey carrying Mary along a desert road at dusk; Flurry hops along behind in a tiny headscarf

Camera: side tracking with the walkers · Sound: hooves, footsteps on gravel

callout: NAZARETH TO BETHLEHEM / FOR A ROMAN CENSUS

1.4 8s

There is no room to stay. So the baby is born in a stable, and laid in a manger.

Warm lantern-lit stable, straw, ox and donkey, Mary and Joseph kneel by the manger

Camera: slow push in · Sound: straw rustle, soft lullaby

1.5 7s

Angels announce a saviour. Shepherds come to see him, and wise men follow a star.

Hillside with shepherds and sheep looking up at a glowing light; three wise men on camels follow the star across the dunes

Camera: pan up to the star · Sound: choir swell, camel bells

1.6 5s

A beautiful story. With one small problem. It never says the date.

Flurry flips frantically through a giant book, then shrugs with both twig arms

Camera: push in on Flurry · Sound: fast page flips, comic boing

chip: NO DATE GIVEN

Act 2 Why 25 December 200 - 336 AD · 62s

2.1 9s

Around the year 200, a scholar called Clement of Alexandria wrote that some people had worked out the exact day.

A scholar writes at a desk piled with scrolls in a sunlit library with columns

Camera: dolly past the scroll shelves · Sound: quill scratching

callout: CLEMENT OF ALEXANDRIA / SCHOLAR, EGYPT

2.2 7s

Their answer? The 25th of the Egyptian month of Pachon. That is around the 20th of May.

A big calendar flips from PACHON 25 to MAY 20; Flurry pops on sunglasses

Camera: push in on the calendar · Sound: page flip, ding

chip: 25 PACHON = 20 MAY

2.3 5s

May! So how did we end up in the middle of winter?

Snow starts falling on Flurry in his sunglasses; he shivers and tugs his scarf tight

Camera: slow pull back · Sound: wind gust, teeth chatter

2.4 7s

The first recorded Christmas was in Rome, on the 25th of December, in the year 336.

Roman temple courtyard at winter morning, people in togas, banners, braziers

Camera: crane down past the columns · Sound: crowd murmur, brazier crackle

2.5 13s

And that date was already a party. It sat right by the winter solstice, the darkest time of the year, when Romans honoured their sun god, Sol Invictus, the Unconquered Sun.

A golden statue with a ray crown on a plinth; the sun rises behind the temple and light sweeps across the crowd

Camera: push in as the sun rises · Sound: gong, warm swell

callout: SOL INVICTUS / THE UNCONQUERED SUN

2.6 8s

Christians already linked Jesus with light. One Bible verse even says, unto you shall the sun of righteousness arise.

A scroll unrolls and its lines glow gold; rays spread from it

Camera: slow push in · Sound: soft choir

2.7 13s

So as Christianity grew in the Roman Empire, the church picked the solstice for the birth of Christ. One historian calls it cosmic symbolism. The day the sun is reborn.

Sun breaks over a snowy horizon; Flurry squints, starts to sweat a little and fans himself with his hat

Camera: wide shot, slow push · Sound: sizzle, warm swell

Act 3 Older Than Christmas PAGAN WINTER · 82s

3.1 6s

Long before Christmas, winter festivals were the biggest parties of the year across Europe.

Snowy pine forest clearing at night, a bonfire, villagers in furs dancing in a ring

Camera: slow orbit around the bonfire · Sound: fire crackle, folk drum

3.2 5s

The Celts brought mistletoe and ivy into their winter celebrations.

A druid in a white robe reaches up into an oak to cut mistletoe; Flurry stands under the hanging mistletoe and looks around, embarrassed

Camera: push in · Sound: snip, giggle

callout: CELTS / MISTLETOE AND IVY

3.3 5s

The Norse and the Anglo-Saxons celebrated Yule. Yes, that Yule.

A long wooden Norse hall in snow with carved dragon gables, smoke from the roof

Camera: crane down to the door · Sound: wind, distant horn

chip: YULE

3.4 9s

They feasted on boar and goat, and burned the Yule log, a real tree trunk, chosen and dragged home for the festival.

Villagers drag a huge log on ropes across the snow into the hall; inside a fire roars and a feast table waits

Camera: tracking beside the log · Sound: log scraping snow, fire roar

3.5 6s

In Rome, the solstice festival of Saturnalia had feasting and gift giving too.

Romans around a long table hand each other small wrapped gifts, laughing

Camera: slow dolly along the table · Sound: laughter, cups clink

callout: SATURNALIA / ROME'S WINTER PARTY

3.6 8s

In Eastern Europe, singers went from house to house for Koleda. That tradition grew into the Christmas carol.

Carol singers with a star lantern walk door to door in a snowy village; Flurry joins the end of the line, music notes float up

Camera: side tracking with the singers · Sound: footsteps in snow, la-la choir

chip: KOLEDA = CAROLS

3.7 9s

And the Christmas tree? Its story starts in medieval Livonia, today's Estonia and Latvia, where German merchants put up decorated trees.

Medieval town square with timber houses; a tree hung with apples and candles in the middle; merchants admire it

Camera: crane up the tree · Sound: market bustle

callout: LIVONIA / TODAY ESTONIA AND LATVIA

3.8 11s

Later, German Protestants brought trees into their homes. The Catholic Church resisted for centuries. The Vatican did not get its first Christmas tree until 1982.

A huge tree rises in a grand square in front of a domed church; Flurry taps his wrist like checking a watch

Camera: low angle push up the tree · Sound: crowd cheer

chip: VATICAN'S FIRST TREE: 1982

3.9 8s

Some customs are religious. In 1223, Saint Francis of Assisi popularised the nativity scene, and it spread across Europe.

A candle-lit church with a small nativity crib; a friar in a brown robe sets a figure down

Camera: slow push in · Sound: candle flicker, soft bells

callout: SAINT FRANCIS OF ASSISI / NATIVITY SCENE

3.10 10s

Even the colours mean something. Red for the blood of Christ, green for eternal life, gold for the gifts of the wise men.

Three giant baubles, red, green and gold, swing down on ribbons and light up one by one

Camera: slow track across the baubles · Sound: three chimes

3.11 6s

Or, if you ask the shops, red for Santa and green for the tree.

Flurry winks, pulls a Santa hat onto his head, a tree slides in beside him

Camera: push in · Sound: wink ding, cash register

Act 4 Santa 280 - 1930s · 97s

4.1 5s

Which brings us to the biggest star of all. Santa Claus.

Spotlight snaps on a snowy rooftop chimney; Flurry drumrolls on a bucket

Camera: push in on the chimney · Sound: drumroll, cymbal

slam: SANTA CLAUS

4.2 8s

His story begins with a real man, Saint Nicholas, born in the late 200s in what is now Turkey.

A sunny Mediterranean town with white houses; a bishop in red robes and a tall mitre walks the street

Camera: tracking beside Nicholas · Sound: seagulls, footsteps

callout: SAINT NICHOLAS / MYRA, TODAY'S TURKEY

4.3 11s

He was known for kindness. It is said he gave away all his inherited wealth to people in need, and he became the protector of children.

At night Nicholas drops a small bag of coins through a window; inside, children wake up and cheer

Camera: slow push to the window · Sound: coin jingle, kids cheer

4.4 6s

His feast day falls in December. So, over time, he got tied to Christmas.

A calendar page shows 6 DECEMBER, slides along to 25 DECEMBER

Camera: lateral slide · Sound: page slide

chip: FEAST DAY IN DECEMBER

4.5 10s

Dutch families brought him to America. In 1773, a New York newspaper reported them honouring Sinterklaas. Say Sinterklaas fast, and you get Santa Claus.

An old newspaper spins in; the word SINTERKLAAS squeezes and morphs into SANTA CLAUS while Flurry says it faster and faster

Camera: spin in, push in · Sound: paper whoosh, squeak

4.6 9s

In 1841, thousands of children lined up at a Philadelphia shop to see a life-size Santa. After that, Santa was everywhere.

An old shop window with a life-size Santa model, a long line of children in coats outside in the snow

Camera: dolly along the queue · Sound: crowd of kids, bell on door

4.7 10s

Early Santas often wore green, blue, or white. Coca-Cola's adverts in the 1930s made the jolly red Santa famous all over the world.

A Santa figure's coat changes colour green, blue, white, then red; Flurry spins dizzy watching

Camera: orbit around Santa · Sound: four magic swishes

4.8 9s

And why the North Pole? Thank the cartoonist Thomas Nast, drawing for Harper's Weekly from 1863. The reindeer came with the address.

Icy North Pole with a striped pole, a reindeer team and a red sleigh; Flurry pats a reindeer

Camera: crane down to the sleigh · Sound: wind, sleigh bells

callout: THOMAS NAST / HARPER'S WEEKLY

4.9 8s

Other countries have their own gift bringers. In Germany and Switzerland, it is the Christkind, an angel-like child.

A glowing golden-haired angel child in white floats over a snowy German street with gifts

Camera: slow push · Sound: soft bells

chip: CHRISTKIND

4.10 6s

In Scandinavia, a little elf called the Jultomte rides a sleigh pulled by goats.

A small bearded elf in a red cap drives a sleigh pulled by two goats through snowy pines

Camera: tracking with the sleigh · Sound: goat bleat, bells

chip: JULTOMTE

4.11 7s

Finland's Joulupukki, the Yule Goat, started out rather scary, before he became a friendly Santa.

A shaggy goat-horned figure in a dark doorway; a puff of snow and he becomes a smiling Santa; Flurry hides, then laughs

Camera: push in · Sound: spooky sting, pop, laugh

chip: JOULUPUKKI = YULE GOAT

4.12 8s

And in Italy, La Befana, a kind old witch on a broomstick, slides down the chimney with toys.

A witch on a broomstick flies over moonlit rooftops and dives into a chimney

Camera: track with the broom · Sound: whoosh, cackle

chip: LA BEFANA

Act 5 Kings And Feasts 800 - 1848 · 82s

5.1 10s

Through the Middle Ages, Christmas came and went. At first, a bigger day was Epiphany, the 6th of January, when the wise men visited.

Three wise men on camels crest a dune at sunrise under the star

Camera: crane up over the dune · Sound: camel bells, wind

5.2 8s

In Spain, it is still the Day of the Kings, and that is when many children open their presents.

Spanish street parade with three kings on a float throwing sweets; children in a living room open gifts

Camera: dolly with the parade · Sound: cheers, music

chip: DAY OF THE KINGS

5.3 6s

Soon December took over. The twelve days of Christmas began, another echo of Saturnalia.

Twelve candles light up one after another along a long table

Camera: track along the candles · Sound: twelve soft ticks

chip: 12 DAYS OF CHRISTMAS

5.4 9s

Kings loved it. Charlemagne was crowned on Christmas Day in the year 800. So was William the Conqueror, in 1066.

A stone church throne room; a crown is lowered onto a king's head; a second king in mail follows

Camera: push in on the crown · Sound: organ chord, cheer

5.5 8s

And in 1377, King Richard the Second threw a Christmas feast where guests ate 28 oxen and 300 sheep.

A huge medieval feast hall, a long table piled with roasts, a tally counting oxen and sheep; Flurry sits at the end looking very full

Camera: slow dolly down the table · Sound: feast chatter, lute

tally: 28 OXEN + 300 SHEEP

5.6 9s

Back then, gifts often went between landlords and tenants, not just family. And they were swapped on the 6th of January.

A lord at a manor door receives a basket from a tenant and hands back a wrapped gift

Camera: slow push · Sound: door creak, coins

5.7 8s

In the 1500s and 1600s, during the Reformation, many Protestants moved gift giving to the 24th and the 25th.

A family by a fire hands out gifts; a calendar slides from 6 JAN to 25 DEC

Camera: push in · Sound: fire crackle, page slide

chip: GIFTS MOVE TO 25 DEC

5.8 6s

Some strict Puritans even banned Christmas for a while. It did not last.

A stern Puritan nails up a BANNED sign; a snowball from Flurry knocks it off

Camera: static wide, then whip to Flurry · Sound: hammer, splat

chip: CHRISTMAS BANNED!

5.9 9s

In Britain, Christmas Day became a bank holiday in 1834. And German-born Queen Charlotte brought the Christmas tree to the royal court.

A Georgian palace parlour; Queen Charlotte in a gown beside a tree lit with candles

Camera: crane down to the tree · Sound: harpsichord, candle flicker

callout: QUEEN CHARLOTTE / GERMAN-BORN QUEEN

5.10 9s

And by 1848, a famous picture of the royal family around their tree made one a must-have in every home.

A gilded picture frame shows a royal family around a tree; it pulls back to many homes with trees in their windows

Camera: pull back from the frame · Sound: music swell

Act 6 Everyone'S Winter TODAY · 63s

6.1 5s

Winter has always been a time to celebrate, whatever you believe.

A snowy town square at dusk full of people, lights strung between houses

Camera: crane down into the square · Sound: crowd, bells

6.2 7s

Jewish families celebrate Hanukkah, the eight-night festival of lights. Its dates move with the Hebrew calendar.

A menorah in a frosty window; candles light one by one

Camera: slow push in · Sound: soft ticks, warm pad

chip: HANUKKAH / 8 NIGHTS

6.3 10s

Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan, and it moves through the year. Fun fact: Islam honours Jesus as a prophet.

Lanterns and a crescent moon over a family dinner table

Camera: slow dolly · Sound: lantern clink, chatter

chip: EID AL-FITR

6.4 7s

Kwanzaa, a celebration of African-American heritage, starts on the 26th of December and lasts seven days.

A kinara with seven candles, three red, one black, three green, lights up on a table

Camera: push in · Sound: soft drum

chip: KWANZAA / 26 DEC - 1 JAN

6.5 9s

And millions of people, of every faith or none, simply enjoy the lights, the food, the gifts and time with family.

Flurry and a crowd of villagers gather around a giant lit tree in the square

Camera: crane up the tree · Sound: cheer, bells

6.6 13s

So that is Christmas. A birthday on a borrowed date. A tree from Livonia. A log from the Norse. Carols from Koleda. And a saint from Turkey in a red suit.

The tree, log, carol star and Santa hat orbit Flurry one after another

Camera: orbit around Flurry · Sound: whoosh per item

6.7 8s

However you celebrate, tell us in the comments how you spend it. And subscribe for more stories like this.

Flurry points at a big glowing subscribe bell that swings in

Camera: push in · Sound: bell ding

6.8 4s

From all of us, and from Flurry... Happy Christmas!

Flurry and the reindeer wave; fireworks burst over the snowy village and HAPPY CHRISTMAS lights up in the sky

Camera: crane back and up · Sound: bells, cheer, fireworks

slam: HAPPY CHRISTMAS!
